claims.text: the request selects BOTH the epoch cell and the payload: with ONE fixed 340-byte image, the 21-byte request chooses the epoch cell T (100, 106 or 112) and the 10-trit payload V written exactly in it and executed there (OUT = V % 256 at pc = T, END at T+1)

the epoch cell is chosen by the request byte, not by the program: mutating ONLY the epoch byte moves the payload from cell 100 to cell 106 (cell 100 keeps the 29524 mask) and changes the opcode from OUT to an invalid one (no output), while mutating ONLY a control digit changes the payload and keeps the epoch

the pointer mechanism needs no comparison by value: the DLOAD reads mem[W] = b, d becomes b, the automatic increment lands on T = b+1 and the CRAZY writes exactly there; the successor cell T+1 serves both as END ((v+T+1)%94 = 81) and as the trampoline back to W (v+1 holds W-1) through a two-DLOAD chain identical in all three epochs
the request is consumed in order: the 21 bytes (1 epoch byte + 20 control digits) are read in sequence and each one lands in its own position
the payload does not spill: the two epoch cells that were NOT selected still hold the 29524 mask at the end of the run
the decomposition V = crazy(M, P) with P = 29524 + sum(3^p for trit_p(V)=1) and M = 29524 + sum(3^p for trit_p(V)!=0), both in {1,2}^10, holds for ALL 59049 words (exhaustive, 0 mismatches)

NEGATIVE: the trit -> control-digit map that would let the request carry the 10 trits directly ((0,2,0) or (0,2,2)) is NOT reachable by any composition of crazy: the semigroup over one trit has exactly 15 maps and neither is among them ((0,0,2) is reachable). The interface therefore carries control digits

the epoch and the payload are coupled (measured): the opcode of V at T is (V+T)%94, so the same word is not the same opcode in another epoch. With the three implemented epochs (residues 6, 12, 18 mod 94) there are 0 residues whose three opcodes are all valid, against 8 for three epochs aligned to 94
the data zone admits 92 candidate epochs (34 <= T <= 126 with a printable successor v = 80-T mod 94 and v+1 <= 126); this pack implements and measures 3 of them
an epoch byte outside the catalogue (measured, no gate) selects no epoch at all: the payload lands in none of the epoch cells

two independent Python engines agree byte for byte with the repo oracle (traced repo oracle + traced native_classic), and the C runner matches byte for byte when the payload is printable (V = 93 at epoch 100: same OUT 0x5d, 218 steps) and stops at the printable guard otherwise (step 217, exactly the step predicted from the oracle trace, see c_printable_guard_v1)
